purpose: Measure full CPU control-loop execution cost and bounded fault behavior against a narrow straight-line reference path.

workload.environment: vare.demo.ToyHooks; four-parameter contextual Bernoulli policy with an analytic deterministic reward oracle
workload.update: CPU REINFORCE-style parameter update in the repository's ToyHooks; not an LLM or pretrained-model update
workload.evaluation_task_generator: vare.demo.make_tasks with disjoint seed range from training
workload.evaluation_reuse: one fresh held-out synthetic cohort per round, paired between incumbent and candidate, never reused in later rounds

shared_dataplane: same seeded tasks and rollout order
same policy initialization and random generator seed
same PrioritizedReplay implementation, capacity, group size, and batch size
same trainer, candidate evaluator, and CPU process configuration
arms.vare: CapabilityLoop with policy/verifier freshness checks, grouped replay rescreening, report validation and PromotionGate, candidate cleanup, and round ownership.
arms.baseline: Straight-line orchestration over the same hooks/replay primitives; no use-time freshness filter, PromotionGate/report validation, candidate ownership, or serialization. It retains a fixed primary point-gain threshold and discards a candidate on an ordinary point-estimate rejection.

promotion.note: PromotionGate still computes paired report diagnostics; the baseline uses only the primary point threshold.

cases: worker_crash: real child process exits via os._exit(73) during rollout; retry the round
stale_rollouts: policy lag 3 and verifier lag 4, beyond locked admission bounds
evaluator_failure: candidate evaluator raises after training
concurrent_execution: overlap two rounds and force a shared-candidate-id race in the reference path
interrupted_promotion: promotion mutates active policy then raises cancellation before acknowledgment
fault_injection.forced_positive_candidate: For evaluator and publication fault paths, a known synthetic positive candidate is constructed to force execution through the targeted boundary; this is a control fault fixture, not a trained capability result.

measurement.process_isolation: performance trials use one fresh child process per arm and seed; the fault matrix runs in one coordinator process and launches a real child only for the worker-exit injection
measurement.arm_order: performance arms alternate by seed parity; fault arms run in fixed baseline-then-VARE order per case
measurement.latency: per-round wall time, p50/p95 over all round samples
measurement.throughput: rollouts divided by full trial wall time
measurement.memory: process peak RSS and tracemalloc peak per isolated trial
measurement.staleness: max rollout and replay-batch policy/verifier version lag
measurement.uncertainty: 10,000-draw percentile bootstrap CI over per-seed throughput and paired VARE-minus-baseline differences
measurement.timing_scope: process setup is outside the timed interval; Python process startup and RSS are recorded separately from pipeline elapsed time
measurement.raw_rows: one JSONL record per isolated arm/seed trial; fault rows are separately retained

claims_boundary: This measures the VARE control path with a deterministic simulated four-weight policy, not a real-model update.
Task performance is not a benchmark endpoint and must not be described as model capability.
The straight-line reference is an in-repository comparator, not an external RL framework or production system.
Results apply only to the recorded host, Python runtime, fixed CPU fixture, and tested fault schedule.
